kurz: How dubious return promises can be recognised by the market price of risk, and what to do if the money has already been transferred.

bloecke.md:
There is a clear line between an expensive product and fraud. With an expensive product, too much is charged, but there is something in return, such as a fund unit, an insurance policy or a share. With fraud, there is nothing in return. There is neither a securities account nor a position nor a counterparty, only a database with figures that someone types in.

Both cost money but call for different responses. Comparison helps against expensive products. Against fraud, the only thing that helps is not paying in any money, because once a transfer has been made, the recovery rate is low. Investment fraud can be recognised because its patterns have hardly changed for decades. Only the channel changes, from the telephone to email to the chat group.

The most effective checking tool is a publicly available figure, namely the price the market pays for risk. It is more reliable than gut feeling.

bloecke.titel: Market yields by risk in September 2026
bloecke.unter: Euro values in euros, US values in dollars. For simplicity, the credit spreads were added to the yield of the ten-year government bond. Returns higher than in the last bar exist only as promises.

bloecke.md:
The values in the chart are enough to put return promises into context. The safest fixed-income security in euros yields 3.52% over ten years. For bonds from companies rated as speculative, the market pays a premium of 2.69 percentage points. Only at the very bottom of the credit rating scale, in the CCC segment, does the calculation arrive at around 15.7%. According to the S&P series from 1981 to 2008, more than 40% of the borrowers in this segment defaulted within a year in crisis years.

This gives a rule that works without any knowledge of the industry. A double-digit return is always a statement about risk. With a reputable offer, this risk is stated openly and described in the prospectus. If, on the other hand, the return is combined with “safe”, “guaranteed” or “capital-protected”, the provider is claiming that it can systematically pay more than the global market pays for the worst borrowers. Such an offer contradicts itself.

bloecke.formel: Claimed risk premium = promised return − safe interest rate
bloecke.erklaerung: The risk-free rate is deducted from the promised return. The remainder is the price that the provider supposedly receives for a risk that it denies at the same time.
variablen: Converted to an annual basis, not read per month
Yield of the German federal bond (Bund) with a matching maturity, September 2026: 3.52% over 10 years
bloecke.beispiel: “5% a month, with no price risk” corresponds to 1.05 to the power of 12 minus 1 = 79.6% a year. The claimed risk premium is therefore around 76 percentage points, although the risk is supposedly zero.

bloecke.md:
## Unsolicited calls and boiler rooms

With cold calling, the contact comes from the provider. It may be a friendly caller, a chat invitation to a “share group” or an advert showing the face of a celebrity who supposedly made their fortune with a platform. Behind this there is often a boiler room. This is a call centre, usually abroad, whose staff work from a script and are paid per deal closed. In the first stage, they never sell a product. They first build a relationship. This includes daily calls, technical jargon and a personal “analyst”.

Two legal rules help with checking. First, every company that provides investment services in Germany needs authorisation (Section 32 KWG, Banking Act; for investment firms Section 15 WpIG, Investment Firm Act). Nobody may operate without an entry in the company database of BaFin (Federal Financial Supervisory Authority) or a proper EU passporting notification. Second, authorised institutions must record telephone investment advice (Section 83(3) WpHG, Securities Trading Act) and keep the recording for five years (Section 83(8) WpHG). Customers can request it until it is deleted (Section 83(7) WpHG). A call centre that does not want to know about a recording is therefore not behaving like an authorised institution. Unsolicited advertising calls to private individuals are prohibited anyway (Section 7(2) UWG, Act against Unfair Competition).

The most common mistake when checking is to look up the name in a search engine and be satisfied that the company exists. Fraudsters copy the names, register numbers and legal notices (Impressum) of genuine institutions (identity misuse, known in the jargon as cloning). Contact details should therefore never be taken from the caller's email or website. It is safer to research them yourself and call that number.

bloecke.titel: How investment fraud unfolds, as described by BaFin
bloecke.unter: Each stage serves a purpose. The small test payout comes from the money that the victim paid in.

bloecke.md: No authorised German institution demands a payment before it pays out. Capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) is withheld from the payout amount and paid over to the tax office (Section 44(1) EStG, Income Tax Act) and is not requested from the customer in advance. A provider that demands tax, a fee, a deposit or an “activation” before the payout has nothing to pay out. From this point on, every further euro is certainly lost.

## Ponzi schemes

A Ponzi scheme pays the returns of existing investors out of the deposits of new investors. As long as the inflow grows, it looks like a functioning fund, with account statements, tax certificates and satisfied customers who recommend it to others. This is what makes such schemes dangerous, because the recommendations come from people acting in good faith.

The collapse is certain; only the timing is open. If each participant has to recruit three new ones, the scheme needs three times as many new participants in each round as in the previous round. After 16 rounds, 64.6 million people would be involved on paper. In round 17, the scheme would need more people for the new entrants alone than Germany has inhabitants. This round is therefore never reached.

bloecke.md:
## Pump and dump and self-interested recommendations

In a pump and dump, a group buys a thinly traded share, then promotes it intensively in forums, chat groups or short videos and sells into the demand this generates. This only works with a low free float and a thin order book, because in such shares even a few tens of thousands of euros move the price by double-digit percentages. Investors who buy after the recommendation do not profit from the tip. They are the buyers to whom the group sells its shares. Market manipulation is prohibited (Articles 12 and 15 of the EU Market Abuse Regulation, MAR) and in Germany is punishable by a fine as an administrative offence (Section 120 WpHG). It is a criminal offence under Section 119 WpHG if it is committed intentionally and thereby affects the stock exchange or market price; the attempt is also punishable.

This must be distinguished from the legal but self-interested recommendation. Under Article 20 of the Market Abuse Regulation, people who publicly make investment recommendations must disclose their identity, separate facts from opinions and state their own positions and any remuneration connected with the recommended security. With portfolio videos and affiliate links, it is therefore less important whether the author is right. The more useful question is whether they are paid when the viewer trades, and whether they earn from the viewer's investment result or from the viewer's trading activity.

punkte: Company name, registered office and register number appear exactly like this in the BaFin company database
Documents state the issuer, rank of the claim, costs and risk of total loss clearly and without sugar-coating
Payment goes to an account in the company's name, not to a private individual
Telephone advice is recorded and handed over on request
Doing nothing has no consequences; nobody calls again in the evening
Double-digit return and a promise of safety in the same sentence

Remote access software is to be installed on your own computer “so that we can set it up together”
Payout only after advance payment of tax, a fee or a deposit

bloecke.md:
## Legal but expensive products

Most financial losses are caused by authorised but expensive products sold by sales networks. Criminal offences are less often the cause. These products include subordinated loans and profit participation rights (Genussrechte) on the grey capital market, direct investments in containers or forests and closed-end investments with high soft costs. What mainly distinguishes them from a bank securities account is their rank. In the event of insolvency, subordinated capital is only served after all other creditors, which in practice usually means not at all. The high interest rate is the price for this risk.

With these products, distribution is paid for out of the investment itself. Financial investment intermediaries (Finanzanlagenvermittler) work with authorisation under Section 34f GewO (Trade Regulation Act) and on a commission basis. Investment service providers may only accept inducements from third parties under strict conditions and must disclose them (Section 70 WpHG). In independent fee-based investment advice (Honorar-Anlageberatung), inducements may not be kept at all (Section 64(5) WpHG). Investors who want to know how an adviser earns money should ask exactly that, directly and before any discussion of products. How the industry as a whole earns money is explained in the last lesson of this module.

bloecke.unter: With Madoff, the steady course of returns was conspicuous, with Prokon the interest rate far above market level; each of these cases could be recognised by its structure.

ereignisse.text: Classic Ponzi scheme over decades with constant returns and no losing year, an unknown auditor and no independent custodian.

Profit participation rights, sold to tens of thousands of private investors and advertised with fixed interest far above market level. Profit participation capital is loss-absorbing and ranked behind the other creditors in the insolvency proceedings.
Direct investment with rental payments and a buy-back promise. A large proportion of the containers sold did not exist, and the buy-backs could only be paid for with money from new sales.
A DAX group and not a grey-market provider. The €1.9 billion in trust accounts did not exist. Regulation and an audit opinion do not replace diversification either.

schritte.text: Search for the provider in the BaFin company database and also check the BaFin warnings and the warning lists of ESMA and IOSCO. The company name and registered office must match character for character.
Research the telephone number yourself and call it. If the caller claims to “represent” a well-known institution, ask that institution directly whether the intermediary exists.

Clarify who the issuer is, who is liable and what rank the claim has. Ask for the key information document or the investment product information sheet (Vermögensanlagen-Informationsblatt). If there is none, the conversation is over.
The recipient's name must match the company name. No private account, no wallet, no payment service in a third country and no cash payment to a representative.
Clarify how, at what price and with what notice period an exit is possible. This must be clarified before the first deposit.

bloecke.md:
1. Stop all further payments immediately. This also applies to the “final fee for activation”.
2. Secure evidence, such as screenshots of the platform, chat histories, names, phone numbers, bank details and transaction IDs.
3. Inform your bank. A recall request is no more than a plea, because a payment order becomes irrevocable as soon as the bank receives it (Section 675p(1) BGB, Civil Code). The refund claim for unauthorised payments (Section 675u BGB) does not apply if the customer authorised the payment themselves. Speed still matters.
4. Secure your access, that is uninstall remote access software, change passwords and TANs and block cards.
5. File a criminal complaint (fraud, Section 263 StGB, Criminal Code; for false statements in prospectuses also Section 264a StGB). The case reference number is a prerequisite for almost all further steps.
6. Report the case via the BaFin whistleblower office (Section 4d FinDAG, Financial Services Supervision Act) and contact the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale). Claims generally become time-barred three years after the end of the year in which the damage and the person responsible became known (Sections 195, 199 BGB).

In a **recovery scam**, a supposed “law firm” gets in touch, offering to recover the money in return for payment in advance. As a rule, the call comes from the same group of perpetrators. The perpetrators exploit the victims' hope of getting their money back.

In addition, tax may be due on gains that never existed. According to established case law of the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH), **fictitious returns** from Ponzi schemes are taxable as capital income (Section 20(1) no. 7 EStG) as long as the operator appeared willing and able to pay at the time of the payout. This also applies if the “credit” was merely reinvested. A tax claim can thus be added to the total loss.

Three rules are enough for protection. If the contact came from outside, caution is called for. If the return is above what the market pays for the worst borrowers, the offer contradicts itself. If money is supposed to flow before the payout, it is fraud.

mitnehmen: A return promise converted to an annual figure, minus the Bund yield, gives the claimed risk premium; in September 2026, the market pays just under 16% even for CCC borrowers.
Providers that are not listed character for character in the BaFin company database may not operate in Germany, however reputable they appear; fraudsters also copy the names of genuine firms.
If a provider demands money for tax, a fee or a deposit before the payout, that is a clear signal to break off, because German institutions withhold the tax from the payout amount.
Ponzi schemes inevitably collapse for mathematical reasons, and a recommendation from satisfied acquaintances is no proof of safety, because it is part of the mechanism.
Losses more often arise by legal means, because subordinated capital and commission-based products cost rank and return without anyone committing a criminal offence.

begriffe.text: Call centre, usually abroad, that sells financial products unsolicited, working from a script and for a commission on each deal closed. It has no authorisation under Section 32 KWG or Section 15 WpIG.
Investment model in which payouts to existing investors come from the deposits of new investors. It inevitably ends, because the required inflow grows exponentially.
Driving up the price of a thinly traded security through coordinated promotion, followed by selling into the demand this creates. It is market manipulation under Articles 12 and 15 MAR.
Second fraud against the same victim. Recovery of lost investment money is offered in return for payment in advance, usually by the same group of perpetrators.
Income credited but not actually earned in a Ponzi scheme. According to BFH case law, it can nevertheless be taxable (Section 20(1) no. 7 EStG).
